title: Splenocyte
source:
{{cs1 config|name-list-style=vanc|display-authors=6}}
'''Splenocytes''' are white blood cells that reside in the spleen and are involved in functions of the spleen, such as filtering blood and the immune response.<ref name="Cleveland_Clinic">{{Cite web |title=Spleen: Function, Location & Size, Possible Problems |url=https://my.clevelandclinic.org/health/body/21567-spleen |access-date=2024-03-26 |website=Cleveland Clinic |language=en}}</ref>

Splenocytes consist of a variety of cell populations such as T and B lymphocytes, dendritic cells and macrophages, which have different immune functions.<ref name="Bronte_2013">{{cite journal | vauthors = Bronte V, Pittet MJ | title = The spleen in local and systemic regulation of immunity | journal = Immunity | volume = 39 | issue = 5 | pages = 806–818 | date = November 2013 | pmid = 24238338 | pmc = 3912742 | doi = 10.1016/j.immuni.2013.10.010 }}</ref>

== Overview ==
[[File:Illu_spleen.jpg|thumb|An image of the spleen in the human body. Also shows the red and white pulp regions.]]
Splenocytes are spleen cells and consist of [[White blood cell|leukocytes]] like [[B cell|B]] and [[T cell|T cells]], [[Dendritic cell|dendritic cells]], and [[Macrophage|macrophages]].<ref name="Bronte_2013" /> The spleen is split into [[Red pulp|red]] and [[White pulp|white pulp regions]] with the [[marginal zone]] separating the two areas. The red pulp is involved with filtering blood and recycling iron, while the white pulp is involved in the immune response.<ref name="Bronte_2013" />

The red pulp contains macrophages that [[phagocytosis|phagocytose]] old or damaged red blood cells.<ref name="Cleveland_Clinic" />

The white pulp contains separate compartments for B and T cells called the B cell zone (BCZ) and the T cell zone (TCZ).<ref name="Lewis_2019">{{cite journal | vauthors = Lewis SM, Williams A, Eisenbarth SC | title = Structure and function of the immune system in the spleen | journal = Science Immunology | volume = 4 | issue = 33 | date = March 2019 | pmid = 30824527 | pmc = 6495537 | doi = 10.1126/sciimmunol.aau6085 }}</ref> B cells make antibodies to fight off bacterial, viral, and fungal infections, and T cells are activated in response to antigens.<ref name="Cleveland_Clinic" /><ref name="Bronte_2013" /><ref name="Lewis_2019" />

The marginal zone (MZ) separates the red and white pulp regions and contains macrophages, B cells, and dendritic cells. MZ macrophages remove some types of blood-borne bacteria and viruses.<ref name="Bronte_2013" /> MZ B and dendritic cells are involved in antigen processing and presentation to [[Lymphocyte|lymphocytes]] in the white pulp.<ref name="Bronte_2013" />
